criterion: The project archive mixes full-width tiles with half-width pairs down one authored order.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the archive lays its fifteen projects down the page in a fixed order whose tile widths alternate between the full page width and a half-width pair. Answer no when every tile is the same width, or when a sort control lets a visitor change the order.

criterion: The home route holds its manifesto sentence still for two full screens of scrolling.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the manifesto sentence stays pinned in place while the document travels under it for about two screen heights before the project run arrives. Answer no when the sentence scrolls away with the page, or when the block it sits in is roughly one screen tall.

criterion: The navigation bar carries three words only: PROJECTS, SIGNALS, CONTACT.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the bar at the top right carries those three uppercase words as its whole contents, with the studio wordmark at the top left standing as the way home. Answer no when a fourth destination appears in the bar, when a dropdown opens from one of the three, or when a home link joins them.

criterion: Every control on the site is the same outlined bar whose fill rises from below when pointed at.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the navigation controls, the archive filters, the tile labels, the form submits and the reel controls are one repeated bar with a hairline outline whose block of ink rises from beneath on hover. Answer no when two or more distinct control shapes appear, or when a control lights up by changing its own text colour alone.

criterion: A reel row moves to a new position by a pointer drag, by a long press on touch, or by an arrow key from its focused handle.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when all three inputs move a row to the same new position on the reel route. Answer no when reordering works by pointer alone, or when the keyboard path moves focus somewhere else instead of moving the row.

criterion: A failed save leaves the client's typed text in the field that received the typing.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a note or a brief whose write fails keeps the characters the client typed, with a message in the strip at the foot of the window offering another attempt. Answer no when the field reverts to an older stored value, or when the failure is silent.

criterion: The studio queue refreshes itself for a watching curator, pausing whenever the browser tab sits in the background.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a reel sent from another session appears in the queue within about half a minute with the tab in front, and the queue stops asking for updates once the tab is hidden. Answer no when the queue needs a manual reload, or when the queue keeps polling behind a hidden tab.

criterion: The archive filter row pans sideways under a finger on a narrow window, springing back when pulled past its start.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the row of five filter controls can be dragged horizontally at a phone width and returns from an overdrag to its resting position. Answer no when the row wraps onto a second line, or when it stops dead at its edge with the overhanging controls unreachable.

criterion: A visitor pressing Add before signing in returns from the sign-in surface to the project pressed, with that project already in the reel.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when pressing Add on an archive tile while signed out opens the sign-in surface, and creating an account returns the visitor to the archive with that tile's control reading Added. Answer no when the visitor lands somewhere other than the address pressed, or when the held add is dropped so the project has to be found again.

criterion: A signed-in client who asks for a studio address stays at that address, reading a refusal screen that offers a way back to their own reel.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the address bar still shows the studio address asked for, the screen reads Not your reel, and a control leads back to the client's own reel. Answer no when the client is redirected somewhere else, or when a blank page with a number on it appears instead of a designed screen.

criterion: The home route, the archive, the journal all sit on one near-black ground carrying near-white text with one red accent.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the whole product reads as three inks, a near-black ground, near-white text and one red accent, with the footer and the mobile panel taking that red as their whole field. Answer no when a fourth colour family appears anywhere, or when the red is used often enough to read as decoration rather than as the brand.

criterion: Every corner on the site is square, with the only soft effect a frosting behind each control bar.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when fields, controls, panels and thumbnails all carry square corners, nothing casts a shadow, and a hairline outline stays legible over a bright moving picture because the bar behind it frosts what it covers. Answer no when a rounded corner or a shadow appears, or when a white hairline disappears over a bright background.

criterion: A headline uncovers itself as a soft window travels up through its letters, reversing when the page scrolls back.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a headline entering view is revealed by a soft-edged band travelling upward through the words, each line starting a beat after the line above, and scrolling back up un-reveals the same headline. Answer no when the headline fades or slides in, or when scrolling back up replays the reveal from its start.

criterion: Every focusable control shows a focus treatment distinguishable from its hover treatment.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when tabbing through a route shows a visible focus treatment on every control, text field and link, and that treatment reads as different from what the same element does under a pointer. Answer no when a focused element looks identical to a hovered one, or when focus visibility is removed anywhere.

criterion: At a phone width the three navigation words collapse into one square button that opens a full red panel.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a narrow window shows one square menu button in place of the three navigation controls, and pressing it wipes a full-screen red panel down over the page with its rows settling a beat behind the wipe. Answer no when the three controls stack or shrink instead, or when the panel pushes the page rather than covering it.

criterion: Small uppercase lettering appears in the brand red on the near-black ground.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a label-sized run of uppercase text is set in the brand red directly on the near-black page ground, such as a practice-field numeral, a section label word or the way home on the wrong-address screen. Answer no when every label-sized run on that ground is set in the near-white ink, leaving the red to the display type, the diagonal and the marks.

criterion: A spinning loader appears on the newsletter field waiting for its request.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the newsletter field in the footer, or any other pending surface in the product, shows a rotating loader rather than the three dots the pending vocabulary uses. Answer no when every pending control shows three dots and the product carries no rotating loader anywhere.
